data.title: The Algorithmic Barrier: Quantifying Frictional Unemployment in Automated Recruitment (Fofanah, 2026)
data.summary: Benchmarks a legacy keyword-based ATS parser against a proposed semantic matching system on the same applicant pool. The legacy system's recall is 0.45 (vs. 0.92 for the semantic system) — meaning most qualified candidates in the pool are never surfaced to a reviewer. The paper's error-mode analysis attributes over 40% of the legacy system's false negatives to pure lexical variation: a candidate's CV describing work in different wording from the posting's exact required terms (e.g. "client engagement" where the rubric expects "customer success"), not a genuine skills gap.
data.citation: Fofanah, I. D. (2026). The Algorithmic Barrier: Quantifying Artificial Frictional Unemployment and Information Asymmetry in Automated Recruitment Systems. arXiv:2601.14534.
